analysis.title: Same Tantrum, Different Decade: The 10Y Has Matched 2013, OATs Are Flirting With 2011, And Stocks Don't Care (Yet)
key_insights: Goldman's Jay Narain (Oct 4) says the US 10Y has risen ~133 bps from its February 2026 low of 3.95% to its September 2026 high of 5.29%, almost identical to the ~137 bps rise in the 2013 taper tantrum.

A fourth straight session of global DM sovereign selling took US 10s to 5.33% and 30s to 5.67% in Thursday's European morning, the highest for both since 2002. Gilts, OATs and BTPs also printed multi-decade marks.
Pasquariello notes the 10Y backed up 82 bps in Q3. Japan's 10Y JGB is at 3.085% against the US 10Y at 5.26% on the same Bloomberg screen.

France is the epicenter in Europe. OAT-Bund reached 141bp on Oct 1, up from 55bp in February. The 2011 peak was ~190bp on Nov 15, 2011. Narain says the speed of widening is comparable to the early stages of 2011.

Goldman's Rates MarketStrats ranks IT 10y vs GE as the biggest weekly mover (+0.21%, 7.2 standard deviations). Privorotsky says that if BTPs move with OATs, the market is pricing European sovereign risk, not just French fiscal risk.
Goldman credit strats (Avishek Biswas) recommend buying protection on the iTraxx SubFin index as a European sovereign risk-off hedge.

Goldman European economists (Stott) estimate France's financial conditions index has tightened 50bp since Aug 1, one of the largest 2-month moves since 2000. They cut French growth to 0.4% this year and 0.6% in 2027, from 0.7%.

France's current account was balanced over the last four quarters, and domestic government debt is only 2% of banks' assets in France versus 5% to 8% in the euro-crisis countries, so there is no doom loop yet.

Goldman European economists (Stehn, Stott) say TPI activation would require significantly more intense and broad-based sovereign stress with inflation well above target. They say addressing fundamental sovereign risk needs a fiscal rather than an ECB solution.

Goldman rates strategists (Cole, Marshall) argue financial conditions tightening tilts the scales toward long US and German duration and see an asymmetry toward lower yields. The next inflation print is the key test for the Fed path.
September payrolls rose 29k against a 90k median forecast (Goldman 80k), with the prior two months revised down. Unemployment rose to 4.2% and average hourly earnings gained 0.1%.

Goldman economists moved their next Fed hike from October to December and see a strong chance the FOMC concludes further hikes are unnecessary. October hike odds fell from above 70% to below 30% over the week.
Goldman futures strategist Robert Quinn says CFTC Non-Dealers sold S&P futures for a fifth week in six through Sept 29 and expects ongoing challenges until yields convincingly reverse.
In Thursday's 10-20Y Treasury buyback, Treasury bought its full $6bn while over $46bn was offered, versus roughly $10.5bn of offers at each of the previous two long-end buybacks.

Will Marshall (Goldman rates) says AI-related issuance is not obviously the specific cause, but investment plans being rate insensitive weighs on duration risk appetite. He sees risks to long-term yields skewed up while borrowing needs grow, with fundamental catalysts needed to revive duration demand.

Goldman expects $420bn of global direct IG issuance from hyperscalers in 2027, up from $400bn, with 35% of 2027 hyperscaler capex debt-funded. 2026 hyperscaler issuance is projected at $250bn, versus sub-$20bn in 2024.
Hyperscalers are about 40% of the more than $575bn of global AI-related debt Goldman has tracked this year. Interest expense is a very small portion of their earnings.

ZeroHedge's tracker shows hyperscaler off-balance-sheet liabilities of $3.8 trillion as of Sept 30, up $700bn from June 30. It says Q3 DV01 issued by the AI ecosystem was about 25% higher than all Treasury issuance.
Hyperscaler issuers are shortening maturities: 29.9% of 2026 issuance was in the 0-5Y bucket from January to June, versus 46.4% since June.

Goldman IG trading desk expects Q4 gross IG supply of $330bn and only $34bn net, after $211bn to $317bn of net supply in each of the first three quarters. Data center deals have been put on hold given the borrowing cost spike. 2027 IG supply is expected to be higher than 2026.
The IG index yields 6.05%, above 6% for the first time since 2023.
Pasquariello's Q3 scorecard: Magnificent Seven +11%, cap-weighted S&P +2%, equal-weight S&P -2%, Russell -8%.

Privorotsky says US equities compartmentalized the rates blowup. Brian Garrett says SPX spot is no longer the clearing price for risk and that equities trade the Fed while bonds trade the regime. Credit and rates signal high anxiety while VIX grinds low.
Goldman's IG desk says AI capex has been more or less the sole driver of IG spread widening, while the AI universe has single-handedly supported equities near record highs.
Pasquariello views higher rates as a headwind to stocks, not a wrecking ball, absent an inflation surge or a credit problem. His Q4 question is whether mega-cap tech can stay duration resistant.

This week's test is the coupon cycle (3s Tuesday, 10s Wednesday, 30s Thursday per the desk's Tuesday-through-Thursday framing) with FOMC minutes on Wednesday. The Sep 23 5Y auction tailed by the second-biggest margin on record.

sector_views.rationale: The AI universe has single-handedly supported the market near record highs, and Q4 hinges on whether mega-cap tech stays duration resistant.
The Russell fell 8% in Q3 while the Magnificent Seven rose 11% and equal-weight S&P fell 2%.

macro_indicators.reading: 5.33% (Thursday European morning high); 5.29% September high per Narain; 5.26% on Pasquariello's Oct 2 screen
macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since 2002 and matches the ~133-137 bp rise of the 2013 taper tantrum.
Highest since 2002 after four straight sessions of global DM bond selling.
Shows the rate selloff is global.
Up from 55bp in February, about two-thirds of the way to the ~190bp 2011 peak.
Weak print with prior two months revised down, which lowered October Fed hike odds.
Rose in September, supporting the case that further hikes are unnecessary.
Soft wage growth adds to the case for lower yields.
Market pricing fell sharply over the week after the payrolls miss.
Tighter financial conditions are cutting growth forecasts.
Above 6% for the first time since 2023.
A near-term supply breather, not a cure, since 2027 supply is expected to be higher.

trade_ideas.description: Buy protection on iTraxx SubFin index as a European sovereign risk-off hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman credit strats see European sovereign stress spreading beyond France.
Financial conditions tightening and widening credit spreads bound the selloff, with an asymmetry toward lower yields.
trade_ideas.risk: Next inflation print and continued AI-related issuance keep upward pressure on long-term yields.

risk_factors: Tight coupon auction cycle this week (3s, 10s, 30s) after the Sep 23 5Y auction tailed by the second-biggest margin on record.
Rate-insensitive AI borrowing, including a projected $420bn of hyperscaler IG issuance in 2027.
European sovereign contagion from France to Italy with no ECB backstop for fundamental sovereign risk.
Inflation surge or a credit problem could turn higher rates into a wrecking ball for equities.
Mega-cap tech failing to stay duration resistant in Q4.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman rates strategists say financial conditions tightening, widening credit spreads and weak payrolls (29k) bound the selloff, with an asymmetry toward lower yields and a Fed that may not need more hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's credit floor counts $420bn of rate-insensitive hyperscaler issuance in 2027, so risks to long-term yields stay skewed up, and Treasury buyback offers and the 5Y auction tail show weak duration demand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak result in this week's 10Y and 30Y coupon auctions, as with the Sep 23 5Y second-biggest tail, would undercut the case that yields are capped.

tension_points.bull_case: Pasquariello views higher rates as a headwind, not a wrecking ball, absent an inflation surge or a credit problem, and AI has supported the market near record highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit and rates signal high anxiety and SPX is no longer the clearing price for risk, with equal-weight S&P and Russell down in Q3.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An inflation surge or a credit problem would turn higher rates into a wrecking ball for stocks.
